after.eli5: Washouts usually come after the market has already fallen. SPY was usually higher 3–6 months later, but days with the same drop did just as well, so the bounce comes from buying lower, not from breadth itself. Often it dipped further first. This one came with the index near its high: past cases like it got there in 6 months, on a bumpier road.
after.src: Table: this page’s 50-day line and SPY closes (price only), about 1, 3 and 6 months later; a horizon still in the future shows –. Study tiles: the 2013+ study: 23 washouts, 3-month median +6.2% (17 of 22 up) vs +4.3% any day; days with a similar fall did +6.4%. 2021+ alone: +9.0%, up 6 of 9. Few cases; describes, does not predict.

thin.sub: When QQQ is near its high but few Nasdaq-100 stocks are above their 200-day, a big drop has followed more often
thin.asof: as of the Oct 2 close · Nasdaq-100 breadth and QQQ update after each close
thin.l2: Thin-rally days in the past year: 142
thin.cap: How often a day with QQQ near its high was followed by a big drop within 3 months, by Nasdaq-100 breadth. Bars: 2013+ · small figures: since 2021 · all near-high days: 17%
thin.ct: QQQ since 2013 (log scale) · red dot = the start of a big drop from its high · amber strip = thin-rally days
thin.how: Plain counts, not a forecast. When QQQ was near its high, a big drop followed within 3 months on 37% of days with thin breadth, against 8% with broad breadth (2013+). Since 2021 the middle band did worst (24% / 32% / 6%), so the steady part is that broad rallies rarely broke. 13 separate stretches, 5 led to a drop. Context for sizing risk, not a sell signal.
thin.now: QQQ is at its 52-week high and only 58.4% of Nasdaq-100 stocks are above their 200-day. This thin stretch began May 13, 2025 and has already seen two big drops (Mar 27 and Jul 29, 2026).
thin.src: Plain counts, not a forecast. History: TradingView’s official Nasdaq-100 breadth to Oct 1, 2026; after it, our live count of today’s members. QQQ closes are split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted.

thrust.sub: A thrust is when the share of Russell 2000 stocks above their 50-day jumps from washed-out to strong within a few weeks
thrust.asof: as of the Oct 2 close · Russell 2000 breadth and IWM update after each close
thrust.l1: Needs a close at the fire line on or before Oct 22 (14 sessions left).
thrust.now: Armed: the line closed at 27.8% on Oct 2. A close at the fire line by Oct 22 would be a thrust; if not, the window lapses.
thrust.ct: Russell 2000 % above 50-day, last 4 months · yellow band = the window
thrust.ct2: IWM over the 3 months after each past thrust · 13 of 15 up (any 3 months since 2013: 65% up, typical +3%)
thrust.how: ARMED alone has meant nothing. FIRED is the part that mattered: after past thrusts IWM did about 3.5 to 5 points better over the next 3 months than after comparable bounces. Only 15 thrusts since 2013, and most of that gap comes from 2021 on, so treat it as a tilt, not a rule.
thrust.src: History: TradingView’s official Russell 2000 breadth line, which gives the 15 thrusts in the lower chart. The live line is our own count of today’s members and can differ by about a point, so a close call at either line can be a session off. IWM closes split-adjusted.

storms.sub: SPY against its 200-day average · below it, the same VIX has come with bigger moves
storms.l1: A fall of about 6.4% would put it below.
storms.l2: SPY 769.64 · 200-day 720.47. Says how rough, not which way.
storms.cap: grey = what VIX expected · colour = how much SPY really moved the next month (2013+ averages, % a year). VIX usually guesses high.
storms.ct: SPY, last 2 years · red = days SPY closed below its 200-day average
storms.how: VIX is the options market’s guess of how much stocks will move, and it usually guesses high. Above the 200-day, next month’s real moves came in well under it (12.5 against 16.1). Below it they came in only a little under (24.1 against 27.1): at the same VIX, moves below the line ran about 20% bigger. It does not call direction. Bumpier rides, not a sell signal.
storms.now: SPY is 6.8% above its 200-day average: the calm side, where next month’s real moves have come in well under what VIX expected (12.5 against 16.1). It has been above since Apr 8, 2026.
storms.src: Study: SPY against its 200-day average, 2013+ (2,930 days above, 508 below). How much SPY really moved means its realised volatility over the next month, as a yearly rate, against VIX that day. In the 10 breaks since 2013, the next 3 months’ returns were not reliably worse than after comparable days, though the dips along the way were deeper.
